note: Voiceover lines per section. {tokens} are filled from live data at record time (see numbers.json) and each numeric sentence is only spoken once the matching text is on screen.

sections.title: Illustrative scenario: Ananya
lines: Meet Ananya.
Her college is withholding her original certificates.
She files a complaint with the Grievance Cell.
What she can't see: the Regulation Bureau is already acting on the same college.
Two bureaus. Two files. One college. And neither knows about the other.

sections.title: Without / With Samanvay
lines: Today, each bureau sees only its own inbox.
Turn Samanvay on, and it connects the same college across bureaus.
Here, {ww.pairs} matches. {ww.noid} have no AICTE ID at all. And on every one, the name is spelt differently.

sections.title: The pre-action check
lines: Back to Ananya's case.
A Grievance Cell officer is about to ask the college for her certificate records.
Before anything is saved, Samanvay raises AICTE's alert: Potential Overlapping Cases, Coordination Required.
Another bureau already asked. The Regulation Bureau requested the same records {check.days} days ago.

sections.title: Coordinate, and the other bureau is told
lines: So the officer coordinates instead.
A note goes to the Regulation Bureau, and the request to the college is held. The college is asked once.
On the other side, the Regulation Bureau's bell rings, and the note is waiting at the top of their inbox.

sections.title: One merged timeline
lines: On the college page, each bureau has its own thread.
Once an officer confirms it's the same college, the threads join into one shared timeline.

sections.title: Reports dashboard
lines: For senior officers, one dashboard shows every bureau's pending, ageing and overdue cases together.

sections.title: Stress test
lines: Names are the hard part.
Here is one college, written {stress.total} different ways, run through the real matcher, live.
Samanvay catches {stress.samanvay}. An exact-name search catches {stress.exact}. An AICTE ID search catches {stress.id}, because these complaints have no ID.
The {stress.misses} misses are shown in red, not hidden.

sections.title: Baselines and accuracy
lines: Across {base.overlaps} planted overlaps, an AICTE ID search finds {base.id}.
An exact-name search finds {base.exact}, with {base.exact_wrong} wrong matches.
Samanvay finds {base.samanvay}, with {base.samanvay_wrong} wrong.
And on a second dataset it was never tuned on, Samanvay again found {seed43.found} of {seed43.overlaps}, with {seed43.wrong} wrong.
A caution: this is synthetic data we made ourselves. Real complaints will be messier, and every match is only a suggestion until an officer confirms it.

sections.title: How it works
lines: How it works.
First, an AICTE ID match, when both complaints carry one.
Without an ID, fuzzy name and address matching, which handles initials and abbreviations.
Description similarity tells whether two complaints are about the same issue.
Then rule-based clash checks, before an action goes out.
Explainable rules, no black-box AI, and a person always decides.

sections.title: Inbox, privacy and deadlines
lines: Each officer gets one coordination inbox: notes waiting, clashes prevented, new matches.
And a bureau never sees another bureau's complainant names.
Overdue and due-soon cases alert each bureau, using demo time limits, not official ones.

sections.title: Close
lines: Samanvay checks across bureaus at the moment an officer is about to act.
